_about: Echo Reconstruction (V2): the player gathers clues (echoes and observations), then answers one question about what happened. Each entry is self-contained, so any area can add its own. A clue shows once its 'when' condition holds; every clue marked 'required' must be found before answering. A wrong answer names the clue that rules it out and is crossed off: no penalty, no lost progress. The right answer sets 'solved_flag'. Open a board from dialogue with {"event": "reconstruct", "args": ["<id>"]}.

well_promise.title: The Forgotten Promise
well_promise.intro: Three things at the well remember more than Tobin does.
well_promise.question: What did Tobin promise Elsie?

clues.title: Her voice in the stone
clues.text: TOBIN and ELSIE, carved together. Her voice: "You promised you'd wait for me."

clues.title: The lamp she hung
clues.text: "If I can see a light from the road, I can find the way back."
clues.missing: One lamp in the square is tended more than the others.

clues.title: The worn bench
clues.text: Worn smooth at one end, wax on the armrest, facing the road. Someone waited here every night.
clues.missing: Something by the well has been used every night for years.

clues.title: Tobin's habit
clues.text: Lights the well lamp twice a night. "Never knew why."

answers.text: To marry her when the harvest was in.
answers.feedback: Two names on a well could mean a wedding. But her voice never asked for one. She asked him to wait.

answers.text: To leave Dawnmere with her before the mist came.
answers.feedback: Then nobody would have worn that bench smooth. Someone stayed behind and watched the road.

answers.text: To keep a light burning by the well until she found her way home.
To forget her if she never came back.
answers.feedback: Someone still tends that lamp more than any other. He never stopped keeping the promise. The forgetting was done to him.

well_promise.solved_line: That's it. That's what the lamp is for.

watchman_promise.title: The Watchman's Token
watchman_promise.intro: An iron token, a chair that faces the window, a post at the bridge head.
watchman_promise.question: What was the Watchman waiting for?

clues.title: The token
clues.text: Two initials scratched into iron: E., and one worn away by a thumb.
clues.missing: Something small was left behind in the watchhouse.

clues.title: The chair by the window
clues.text: A child: "Will you still be here when I come back?" The guard: "Until the last lantern goes out."
clues.missing: The chair facing the window remembers something.

clues.title: The post by the bridge
clues.text: Someone waiting by the lit post. A small figure on the road. The bell. Then nothing.
clues.missing: The old post at the bridge head remembers something.

clues.title: The wall
clues.text: Nights counted in fives, hundreds of them, until they stop.

answers.feedback: He made his promise to a child, not to a superior. "Until the last lantern goes out."

answers.text: A signal to close the bridge.
answers.feedback: He kept the lantern lit and watched the road for someone coming, not for a sign to shut it.

watchman_promise.solved_line: Someone was coming home. The bell rang before they arrived.
